summary: Weekly POC check-in focused on early token latency (TTFT) and streaming behavior. SE presented microburst test results showing improved median but persistent 99th percentile spikes for long sequences. Team discussed kernel profile toggles, KV cache warm strategies, and a hybrid hedging plan. Next actions: run microburst with new flags, share logs and pricing update, schedule a short benchmark replay next week.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-29 10:30 AM PT - duration 48 minutes
Attendees: Erin Cole (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood SRE), Mason Liu (Redwood SE), Sofia Kim (Avalon PM), Ravi Patel (Avalon Infra), Leah Torres (Avalon ML), Tom Anders (Avalon CTO), Jamal Greene (Avalon QA)

00:00 Erin Cole: hey everyone thanks for hopping on appreciate it. quick agenda — go over last week's microburst numbers, try the new kernel hedging suggestion, and decide on next benchmark run. if anyone needs extra time flag now.
00:22 Sofia Kim: sounds good erin. i just wanna say we've had a couple of escalations from the merchant checkout team, 95th p95 on live is creeping up during promo windows. so this is high priority.
00:35 Erin Cole: got it, that's consistent with what the logs showed. diego, can you walk us through the test results you uploaded?
00:42 Diego Ramos: yeah sure. so i re-ran the microburst profile with the earlier quantized model and the sequence-length sampler we discussed. median first token latency dropped 12% to about 42ms but the 99th stayed around 420ms in the worst runs. there were these long tail spikes when sequence length hit above 700 tokens, appears to trigger a slower kernel path. note: some transcripts for the run show K-V cache warmups failing initially, might be mis-config on the test harness.
01:12 Leah Torres: when you say slower kernel path, is that the matmul fallback or the TF32 path?
01:18 Diego Ramos: it's the matmul fallback — we saw kernel selection flip at about 512 sequence threshold, which on that architecture picks a more conservative matmul kernel that's stable but slower. also on streaming we saw handshake delays when the prefix chunking didn't align with the batching window.
01:40 Mason Liu: one wildcard is the early token fastpath. in some cases the runtime doesn't take the fastpath because the prompt has a long system message, so initial tokens still go through the general path. we suggested trimming system tokens at callsite or precomputing them into the KV cache. the precompute flow in the private deployment is fine but on hosted we saw some delays with cold cache for new sessions.
02:05 Ravi Patel: mm-hmm. for staging we do rotate nodes nightly which probably evicts caches. we can change to a 72-hour rotation during the POC to keep warm.
02:15 Priya Nair: note on rotation: if you keep nodes longer you need to watch GPU memory fragmentation, but it's doable for the pilot.
02:22 Tom Anders: i'd rather not change rotation without understanding cost; can we see numbers on cost vs latency improvements?
02:28 Erin Cole: yes erin: we'll include burst capacity cost in the pricing sheet. mason can you capture an estimate?
02:34 Mason Liu: sure. rough estimate — keeping warm nodes increases reserved GPU hours by about 8% which for your projected traffic is approx $1.2k a month, plus marginal infra. i'll include a model in the spreadsheet.
02:47 Sofia Kim: ok good. back to the 99th spikes — what about hedging to a smaller model for those long sequences? could that be transparent?
02:56 Diego Ramos: we prototyped an automatic hedging rule: if seqlen>512 and predicted tail > 300ms then route to a quantized variant that uses an alternate kernel optimized for long context. tradeoff is slight quality regression; i put the delta at ~0.6 BLEU-ish on our test prompts but for generation quality that roughly maps to a small behavioral difference.
03:22 Leah Torres: do we have a rollback plan if customers notice hallucinations?
03:26 Diego Ramos: yes, the routing is canaryed and we can return to primary model on error or degrade gracefully to a safe shorter answer with a fallback message. also eval hooks can alert us of quality regression.
03:38 Jamal Greene: from qa — the replay harness should include session-level traces and split by user bucket. we found one QA case where a long prompt plus system assistant role caused the runtime to pick a slower kernel always. might be prompt engineering.
03:55 Diego Ramos: noted — we'll add prompt bucketing.
04:02 Erin Cole: quick check — the microburst CSV in the drive, who's reviewed it?
04:06 Leah Torres: i skimmed it; i can run a filtered view for sequences >600 and post highlights.
04:11 Erin Cole: perfect, please do.
04:14 Sofia Kim: another observation: streaming handshake latency seems proportional to chunk size; we're currently at 1k tokens chunking for streaming. does reducing chunk size hurt throughput?
04:24 Diego Ramos: yes smaller chunk size increases call overhead and slightly reduces throughput but helps early response. there's a sweet spot at ~256 tokens for your workload where TTFT improves and throughput drop is minimal. we can simulate throughput loss — i have a parameter sweep to share.
04:40 Ravi Patel: what's the expected throughput impact? our concurrency target is 250 rps during peak.
04:45 Diego Ramos: estimate is 6–9% throughput reduction at 256 token chunking vs 1k, but TTFT median improves 15–18ms. 99th can also improve because you avoid batch wait times that accumulate.
05:02 Tom Anders: okay so tradeoffs are clear. i want the plan to be: 1) hedging for seqlen>512 2) reduce chunk to 256 in a canary 3) extend node rotation to 72h for warm cache; review after a 48h run. thoughts?
05:20 Priya Nair: operationally fine, but we need metrics to guard — set thresholds for CPU/GPU memory and a rollback for fragmentation.
05:28 Erin Cole: agree. diego, can you propose specific perf thresholds and a rollback signal?
05:33 Diego Ramos: propose: abort canary if p95 latency increases >10% vs baseline, or GPU mem fragmentation causes swap >2% for more than 10 mins. i'll draft exact probes.
05:47 Sofia Kim: also include error rate threshold; last week we had a small increase in 5xx during throttling. rollback on 5xx>0.5% sustained for 5 mins.
05:58 Diego Ramos: good call.
06:01 Erin Cole: quick note on kernel flags — we tested -fastpath and -altmatmul on the bench. -fastpath yields best median but had odd 99th outliers in two runs. -altmatmul stabilized the tail but raised median by ~8ms. recommendation: try a hybrid strategy where we enable -fastpath for short sequences and -altmatmul for long ones.
06:26 Leah Torres: in the last run some transcripts show the runtime mis-identifying token boundaries, transcription had K-V spelled 'K V' a few times, so watch for tokenization mismatch in the sampler.
06:36 Diego Ramos: thanks — that's probably the harness. i'll normalize tokenizer configs across runs.
06:42 Jamal Greene: practical q: when you route to hedged model do you change the response format? our downstream parsers are brittle.
06:48 Diego Ramos: no, we keep schema identical; only difference is model weights and maybe slight length differences. shouldn't break parsers. we'll run a regression suite.
06:56 Erin Cole: ok let's capture concrete next steps and owners. diego will run a microburst with -fastpath plus hedging rules and the chunk size sweep; share CSV and graphs by Thu 6/3. ravi will export k8s pod details and rotation schedule by Wed 6/2. mason to add burst capacity cost estimate. erin will deliver updated pricing and SOC2 appendix by Fri 6/4. we schedule a short replay on Tue 6/8 to validate.
07:28 Tom Anders: sounds good. any blockers from redwood side?
07:32 Priya Nair: we might need a short pvc for persistent kv cache in staging to emulate warm cache behavior; if avalon agrees we'll coordinate.
07:40 Ravi Patel: i think we can permit a staging PVC for the pilot. i'll confirm with infra by EOD.
07:47 Erin Cole: great, appreciate it. last thing — do we want a follow-up 20-minute bench replay next Tue or Wed?
07:54 Sofia Kim: Tue morning works for our team.
07:58 Erin Cole: all right we'll pencil Tue 6/8 9:30 AM PT. thanks everyone.
08:05 Diego Ramos: thanks, i'll paste the run commands and flags into the channel after the call.
08:10 Erin Cole: and i'll upload the pricing sheet. meeting adjourned.

Notes about transcription: occasional speaker overlap, some product names transcribed as "Red wood" and K-V as "K V". timestamps are approximate.
